scalars.scalar_value: Experience working in psychiatric research environments.

items.item_text: Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
Must be willing to work with both a psychiatric population and an addiction treatment research population.
Must have ready access to reliable transportation and be willing to travel off-site to conduct assessments.
Must be willing to work occasional overtime, weekends or flexible schedule.
Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.

Graduation from high school or a General Education Diploma and two years of laboratory experience or two years of college including courses in the natural, physical or social sciences and one year of laboratory experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience; and knowledge and abilities essential to the successful performance of the duties assigned to the position.
Experience working in psychiatric research environments.
Experience in working with and scoring of clinical rating scales and psychophysiological tests, or willingness to learn.

The UC San Diego Department of Psychiatry ranks among the nation's leading academic psychiatry departments, recognized for its exceptional research enterprise, innovative clinical programs, and outstanding educational training. Our faculty and staff are driving meaningful advances in mental health science, delivering transformative patient care, and shaping the next generation of clinicians and researchers. We offer a collegial, high-achieving work environment where talented professionals are empowered to grow, collaborate, and contribute to work that matters.

Under supervision, the Lab Assistant will assist with a number of duties for research studies focusing on mindfulness and psychedelics as a treatment for addiction and chronic pain within UCSD ONEMIND in the Department of Psychiatry. Major responsibilities will include recruiting, assisting with preparing and deploying substance use assessments, assisting with the administration and scoring of clinical rating scales, psychophysiological assessments, physical measurements, preparation and processing of data charts for computerized entry, and entry of data into clinical research database system; and retention efforts for multiple longitudinal studies, working as part of a research team to retain study participants. Perform other general research tasks, such as: library and computer research, and general administrative and office tasks.
Proficiency using PC's including relational databases, word processing, spreadsheet, and statistical analysis programs.
Must be able to maintain confidentiality.
Willingness to travel to addiction treatment clinics to recruit, consent, and assess participants.
Demonstrated understanding of psychology, substance use disorders, and DSM-V criteria for psychiatric disorders.
Ability to design and maintain logs; develop reports and tables.
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work in a multi-cultural environment.
Ability to sustain careful attention to detail for long periods of time.
Demonstrated skill in organizing, analyzing, managing time, setting priorities and meeting deadlines for multiple tasks.
Proven ability to enter data into relational databases in an accurate and precise manner.
